description: Confidence-based escalation + deterministic rules + hardening + benchmark harness. Adds the MCP-sampling fallback to the client's own LLM when Laya confidence is below threshold or on BLOCKED, the deterministic-rule policy layer (the authoritative laya-ultrafast lesson), safety guards (domain allow-list, no auto-submit on destructive forms), configuration surface, and an offline benchmark harness over local structured-form fixtures. Then the README and final docs. Depends on FEAT-003.
steps: src/autopilot/policy.ts: the deterministic-rule layer applied AROUND the narrow Laya decision (per laya-ultrafast's documented lesson that Laya answers narrow questions well but not the open 'what next?'): (1) fill the values the goal states, mapping each to a field via Laya's narrow target choice; (2) after typing into or opening a control, prefer choosing from the options that just appeared; (3) submit, then open/verify the named item. Rules can override or seed the operation when high-confidence-deterministic, and Laya resolves the narrow element/target choices. Keep this as pure functions over PageState + Decision.

src/autopilot/escalation.ts: when engine.decide returns operationConfidence or targetConfidence below a configurable threshold, or operation==='BLOCKED', escalate via MCP sampling: use the SDK server.createMessage / sampling request to ask the CLIENT's LLM to choose the next step given the compact PageState, then parse its structured answer back into a Decision (source='llm'). Guard/parse the LLM output at this boundary. If the client does not support sampling, fall back to returning BLOCKED with a clear reason (graceful).

Wire policy + escalation into src/autopilot/loop.ts: order is deterministic-rule seed -> Laya narrow decision -> confidence check -> escalate to sampling if low/blocked. Record the decision source in the transcript.

src/config.ts: centralize configuration parsed from env + tool args + constructor options (Boundary Discipline: parse once, hand pure typed config inward): headless/headed, viewport, modelDir/LAYA_MODEL_DIR, repo/subfolder/revision, cacheDir/LAYA_CACHE, executionProviders, confidenceThreshold, maxSteps, LAYA_ENGINE (stub|auto), allowedDomains (domain allow-list), and a destructive-form guard flag.

src/safety.ts: (a) domain allow-list — before browser_navigate and before each Autopilot navigation/submit, reject navigation to a host not on the allow-list when one is configured; (b) destructive-form guard — before an Autopilot auto-submit, detect destructive signals (button/nearby text matching delete|remove|pay|purchase|confirm order|transfer|deactivate, or forms with type=password + a payment-like field) and require explicit confirmation / refuse auto-submit, surfacing the reason. Apply these in the tools and the loop.

test/benchmark/: a small offline benchmark harness (script + a few local structured-form fixtures under test/fixtures/) that runs laya_run_goal with the StubEngine (and, when LAYA_MODEL_DIR is set, the real engine) over each fixture, records per-step correctness and end-to-end success (independent final-page check), and prints a summary table. Include it as 'pnpm run bench'. Add a vitest test asserting the harness reports success on the clean fixtures with the stub.

test/safety.test.ts and test/escalation.test.ts: assert the domain allow-list blocks off-list navigation, the destructive-form guard prevents auto-submit on a fixture with a 'Delete account'/'Pay now' button, and that a low-confidence stub decision triggers the sampling path (use a fake sampling callback that returns a canned Decision and assert the loop consumes it). Assert literal expected outcomes.

README.md: define the product (laya-browser-mcp = superset of Playwright MCP + local sub-100ms Laya decision engine that resolves per-step element/action choices on-device so the client LLM is invoked less). HONEST positioning and limits (fast local decision layer + LLM fallback; strong on clean structured forms ~97.7% per-step, weak on arbitrary real sites ~1 step in 5; NOT a fully autonomous general web agent; DONE is not proof of success). Install/config/usage (pnpm install, playwright install chromium, MCP client config for stdio, env vars). List ALL tools with their schemas (the eight Assist tools + laya_run_goal). Explain Autopilot + escalation (narrow Laya + rules + MCP sampling). Document weights: not bundled, ~1.7GB, Laya.load modelDir/LAYA_MODEL_DIR/LAYA_CACHE, and the web-agent export spike outcome + fallback. LICENSE/attribution: project MIT; Laya weights Apache-2.0 (Convai Innovations); Mind2Web-derived material CC BY 4.0 (Deng et al., NeurIPS 2023, not redistributed). Add a LICENSE file (MIT).
Update docs/PLAN.md to reflect the final architecture, the verified-vs-inferred-vs-guessed ledger, and known risks.
acceptance_criteria: When a decision's confidence is below the configured threshold or operation is BLOCKED, the loop escalates via MCP sampling and consumes the returned Decision (verified with a fake sampling callback in tests); if sampling is unsupported it degrades to a clear BLOCKED result.
The deterministic-rule policy layer seeds/overrides operations per the laya-ultrafast lesson and Laya is used for the narrow target choices.
Domain allow-list blocks navigation to off-list hosts; the destructive-form guard prevents Autopilot auto-submit on a fixture containing a destructive action, surfacing the reason.
Configuration (headed/headless, modelDir, thresholds, allowedDomains, engine selection) is parsed in one place and honored.
pnpm run bench runs the offline benchmark over local fixtures with the stub and reports per-step + end-to-end results; the benchmark test passes.

README.md documents the product, honest positioning/limits, install/config/usage, ALL tool schemas, Autopilot+escalation, weights handling, and correct MIT / Apache-2.0 / CC BY 4.0 attribution; a MIT LICENSE file exists.
verification: Run 'pnpm run typecheck' and 'pnpm run build' with zero errors.
Run 'pnpm run test' and confirm the escalation, safety, and benchmark tests pass offline.
Run 'pnpm run bench' and confirm it prints a per-fixture summary with success on the clean fixtures using the stub engine.
findings: Implemented offline (network not required; stub engine + local fixtures). New modules: src/config.ts (single parse point for env+args+options), src/safety.ts (domain allow-list + destructive-form guard, pure functions), src/autopilot/policy.ts (deterministic-rule seed reusing src/laya/goal.ts heuristics), src/autopilot/escalation.ts (MCP-sampling escalation via server.server.createMessage; capability probed with getClientCapabilities().sampling; injectable SampleFn for tests; graceful BLOCKED when unsupported). Wired the pipeline (rule seed -> Laya narrow -> confidence check -> escalate) into src/autopilot/loop.ts, added destructive-guard + allow-list checks, and a transcript 'note' + 'source' per step. server.ts/index.ts now build from loadConfig and resolve the sampler lazily (client capability is only known after connect). Added fixtures delete-account.html and checkout.html; benchmark harness under test/benchmark/ with 'pnpm run bench' (vitest-powered for a single reliable TS runtime) printing a 3/3 summary table; tests test/benchmark.test.ts, test/escalation.test.ts, test/safety.test.ts. VERIFIED: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1 sampling is McpServer.server.createMessage(params) (result.content is a single {type,text} block) confirmed from installed type decls. DEVIATIONS: (1) Adjusted one FEAT-003 test in test/autopilot.test.ts (the rogue-DONE case) to use a goal WITHOUT field assignments so the new deterministic policy layer does not pre-empt the engine; its intent (DONE is independently verified) is preserved. (2) Goal grammar stops unquoted values at punctuation, so the benchmark login goal quotes the email value; documented in README + PLAN known risks. All green offline: pnpm run typecheck, build, test (51 passed, 2 real-weights tests skipped), bench (3/3, 100% per-step). stdio smoke test lists all 9 tools. POLISH PASS (v1 review follow-up, addresses the 3 review issues): (1) Renamed the benchmark per-step metric from stepAccuracy to opsCoverage everywhere (harness.ts BenchResult field + fn, the 'ops-cov' table column, the summary note, benchmark.test.ts assertion, README bench section, PLAN verified line) so it reads as 'expected-ops COVERAGE' (a subsequence match that does not penalize extra/wrong ops), keeping end-to-end success as the trustworthy signal. (2) Scoped checkDestructiveSubmit's text check to the TARGET control (its name + value + option labels) plus the other actionable-control names, and REMOVED the whole-page state.visibleText match that could false-positive on body copy mentioning 'delete'. Kept the neighbour-control and password+payment signals and the fail-safe direction; delete-account.html and checkout.html still blocked (their target buttons' names match directly), benign search submit still allowed. (3) README destructive-guard section rewritten to state exactly which signals it uses (scoped, not whole-page visible text) and that it covers the Autopilot auto-submit CLICK path only (Assist tools apply no destructive check). PLAN known-risks updated for both the guard scoping and the coverage-vs-precision metric. Re-verified: pnpm run typecheck, build, test (51 passed, 2 skipped), bench (3/3 end-to-end success, 100% expected-ops coverage).
